items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Bar Council of India (BCI) to consider withdrawing the upper age limit prescribed for admission to five-year integrated LL.B [Rishabh Duggal & Anr. v. Bar Council of India & Anr.] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a challenge to the BCI's prescription of the upper age limit. Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain , appearing for the petitioner, argued that the BCI's power to prescribe minimum qualifications under the Advocates Act could not be extended to impose an upper age limit. “The power to impose minimum qualifications, can it ever be converted into an upper age limit? This power itself is missing under the Advocates Act,” contended Hossain. The BCI, however, said the upper age limit was prescribed because most five-year law courses were residential. “We have imposed the upper limit because most of the five-year law courses are residential. However, the Court can determine the age. We also have a three-year law course. If someone wants to study law beyond a certain age, they can do the three-year course. Most three-year law courses are not residential, but five-year law courses are mostly residential,” submitted the BCI. Taking note of these submissions, Justice Bagchi asked whether the residential nature of a course could justify an age restriction. “Not all five-year law courses are residential. See Calcutta University. This is not really a criterion to determine the upper age limit,” held Justice Bagchi. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The BCI's Rules of Legal Education, 2008 had prescribed an upper age limit of 20 years for general-category candidates seeking admission to five-year integrated law courses, with a five-year relaxation for certain reserved categories. The rules also prescribed a 30-year upper limit for the three-year law course, with a similar relaxation. The age restrictions have since been the subject of litigation for several years. The BCI had withdrawn Clause 28 of Schedule III of its 2008 Rules (the provision prescribing the age limit) in 2013, after a one-man committee found that the restriction violated Article 14 (equality before law). However, after subsequent litigation , the BCI revived the age restrictions through a September 2016 circular. The validity of the restrictions has since been challenged before different courts. items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has cancelled the bail granted to a murder accused after he sent various threatening messages to the complainant and his family, including one saying "band baja dunga" [Sourabh Narula v State of Haryana & Anr] Justice Vikram Aggarwal said the accused cannot be permitted to remain on bail because any untoward incident can take place if he is allowed to remain free. "In the considered opinion of this Court, he has violated the most essential condition of the order granting bail by threatening the complainant side," the Court said. Justice Vikram Aggarwal The accused Suresh alias Binni Sardana is accused of having committed the murder of one Shyam Lal, who was the servant of one Mukul, a cousin of the complainant Sourabh Narula. Suresh was granted bail on January 28 by the High Court in the case dating back to June 24, 2023. However, soon after he came out of the prison, the accused allegedly started threatening the accused. Narula then moved the Court. In his petition, the complainant said that he and his father received threatening messages on Instagram and Facebook from the accused. One message to the complainant's sister was flagged in particular. “Band bja dunga iske chakkar me to sabki,” the message said. It could mean that "I will finish all of you because of this". It was also alleged that the accused threatened the brother of accused in person. The accused is also alleged to have threatened the accused that if he deposed against him before the trial court, he would upload photographs of his sister on social media. The Court was told that a separate FIR was registered in this regard and the accused is now in custody in that case. In response to the petition, the accused appeared before the Court through video conference, but his behaviour was found to be "abnormal and speech incoherent." The Court said the jail authorities should get his mental state examined, if so required. Considering the nature of allegations against him, the Court cancelled his bail. Advocate Pranshul Dhull represented the petitioner. Senior Deputy Advocate General Vasundhara Dalal Anand represented the State of Haryana. Advocate Samay Sandhawalia represented the accused. items.title: Two coats, one body: Why cheating and criminal breach of trust refuse to share a cell
items.summary: In a Madras courtroom, around a century ago, a man named John McIver stood charged with criminal breach of trust and, as so often happens, with cheating alongside it. What the court did next is worth pausing over: instead of treating the two as interchangeable, it slowed down and told two offences apart. I keep returning to that case - Emperor v. John McIver - for a line of Cornish J’s that has aged well. Reading the word ‘entrustment’ as it sat in the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC), in the context of criminal breach of trust, he reasoned that property got by a trick is never really entrusted at all; and so, in his words, "the same facts will not constitute both criminal breach of trust and cheating". The two are not shades of one wrong. They are different wrongs, built on different foundations. The root of that reasoning lay in the House of Lords’ decision in Lake v. Simmons, where Lord Sumner had stated that a trick preventing true consent leaves no room for entrusting. Honesty compels a fuller picture though, because McIver is not as clear as it appears to be at first blush. McIver had actually been convicted of breach of trust; the Full Bench set the conviction aside on a plea of autre fois acquit , since he had already been acquitted of cheating on the very same facts. However, the judges themselves could not agree on entrustment. Cornish J said that property obtained by deception cannot be entrusted; Mockett and Lakshmana Rao JJ said that it can and that if it can, cheating and breach of trust may both follow. So the notion that the two can coexist on the right facts is no modern heresy. It was in the room from the start. Nine decades on, the distinction remains as relevant as ever and later courts have held it plainly. In Shiv Singh v. State of Rajasthan , the Rajasthan High Court quashed a charge under Section 406 IPC, where cheating had already been ruled out. The reasoning could not be simpler: the two just do not fit together. Cheat someone into parting with property and there is nothing entrusted; entrust something and there was no cheating. Where McIver left the question hanging, Shiv Singh provided the plain answer. The significance of the conjunction ‘and’ Consider almost any economic offence FIR and you will often come across the same pairing: Sections 420 and 406 IPC [now Sections 318 and 316 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS)]. The instinct is easy to understand. Money has gone missing, a client feels wronged, so both provisions go

items.title: Stamping hurdle in enforcement of  arbitral awards
items.summary: Arbitration proceedings ought to resemble a 400-metre race - quick, direct and unhindered. In India, however, they have turned into something closer to a steeplechase, littered with hurdles. The recent judgment of the Delhi High Court in URC Construction (P) Ltd v. Airports Authority of India , pronounced on September 1, 2026, on the stamping of an arbitral award for enforcement proceedings under Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation (A&C) Act, 1996, adds one more such hurdle. The tension between the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 and the A&C Act is not new. Whether a court can appoint an arbitrator under Section 11 of the A&C Act where the agreement is unstamped was hotly debated earlier. In NN Global v. Indo Unique Flame , a Constitution Bench, by a 3:2 majority, held that in case of an unstamped agreement, a High Court can proceed further under Section 11 of the A&C Act only once a certificate has been issued under Section 42(2) of the Stamp Act. In an earlier critique , I had observed that our approach remains rooted centuries back despite technological advancement and developments in arbitration law. Finally, In Re: Interplay between Arbitration Agreements under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 and the Indian Stamp Act , a seven-judge bench held that arbitration clauses in unstamped or inadequately stamped agreements are nonetheless enforceable at the pre-referral stage under Section 11 of the A&C Act. The Court observed that business and commercial entities prefer arbitration because it “obviates cumbersome judicial process, which often prove expensive, complex and interminable”. It held that it is the duty of courts to interpret the A&C Act in a manner that gives life to the principles of modern arbitration in India. The judgment in URC Construction , however, takes a technical approach and fails to reconcile the requirements of the Indian Stamp Act with contemporary legislative advancements and a need to enforce awards expeditiously. URC Construction In URC Construction , the Delhi High Court held that when an inadequately stamped award is produced before the court, the statutory obligation under Section 33 of the Stamp Act to impound the instrument is attracted. It has been held that mere subsequent payment of the deficit stamp duty does not, by itself, cure the defect. items.title: Missing train ticket cannot defeat compensation claim after passenger’s death: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday held that a missing train ticket could not, by itself, defeat a compensation claim by the parents of a man who died after falling from the train [Sukhabhai Nanjibhai Makwana and Another v. Union of India] A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar set aside a Gujarat High Court ruling that had rejected the parents’ compensation claim after finding insufficient evidence that their son had fallen from a train. “ On preponderance of probabilities, it can be concluded that the victim was a bona fide passenger and that absence of recovery of his ticket cannot result in defeating the claim for compensation, ” the Court said. The Bench thus restored the ₹8 lakh compensation awarded by the Railway Claims Tribunal and directed the Railways to satisfy the award within 30 days. Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar The case arose from the death of Maheshbhai, who fell from a train between Sabarmati and Ahmedabad railway stations on September 27, 2017. He suffered serious injuries and died of them on October 31. His parents said he had bought a ticket, but it was lost along with other belongings. In June 2022, the tribunal held that he had been a passenger who suffered an accidental fall. It awarded his parents ₹8 lakh with interest at 9 percent a year from the date of the incident until the date of its order. The Railways challenged the award before the Gujarat High Court. In July 2025, the High Court accepted the appeal and reversed the tribunal decision, citing the absence of a ticket and details identifying the train. Maheshbhai’s parents then approached the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court said the father’s statement on oath that Maheshbhai had bought a ticket shifted the burden to the Railways to rebut the claim. The Bench noted that neither railway witness had checked Maheshbhai’s pockets for a ticket. “ The High Court gave undue importance to the absence of the railway ticket without taking into consideration the statement made on oath by the victim’s father and the fact that the victim had been hospitalised for a period of more than one month ,” the Court said. The Bench added that, while Maheshbhai was undergoing treatment, it was “quite unlikely that the railway ticket would have been preserved by the claimants”. The Court also declined to rely on the Railways’ investigation report, prepared about seven months after the incident without any explanation for the delay. items.title: Supreme Court reserves verdict on plea challenging survey of Sambhal mosque
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday reserved its verdict on a plea filed by the Shahi Jama Masjid Committee at Sambhal challenging a trial court order directing the appointment of an Advocate Commissioner to survey the mosque's premises [ Committee Management, Jami Masjid Sambhal v. Hari Shankar Jain & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe reserved its decision on the plea challenging the Allahabad High Court's May 2025 decision to uphold the trial court's ex-parte order allowing the survey of the mosque's premises. items.title: Kerala court orders FIR against actress Lakshmi Priya for sexually coloured remarks about actress Ansiba Hassan
items.summary: A trial court in Ernakulam has ordered the Palarivattom police to register a First Information Report (FIR) and investigate a complaint accusing actress Lakshmi Priya of making sexually coloured remarks against actress Ansiba Hassan during an interview [ Ansiba Hassan v Lakshmi Priya & ors ]. The dispute concerns an interview given by Priya to online media outlet Can Channel. Hassan claims that the interview included sexually coloured remarks against her, which were intended to outrage her modesty and damage her reputation. She asserted that Priya's comments and the online circulation of such content, amounted to the commission of a cognisable criminal offence. Hassan initially approached the Palarivattom Police seeking action. After the police refused to register an FIR, she approached judicial magistrate first class court in Ernakulam for relief. However, on July 27, the magistrate court dismissed her plea for registration of an FIR, relying on a police report which stated that the allegations did not disclose a cognisable offence and that Hassan could pursue a private complaint for defamation. Hassan challenged the magistrate's decision before the Kerala High Court, stating that her allegations were not confined to defamation and disclosed cognisable offences that required a police investigation. On September 7, the High Court set aside the magistrate's order and ordered the trial court to reconsider the matter afresh. Pursuant to this direction, the magistrate has now directed the Station House Officer(SHO) of the Palarivattom Police Station to register an FIR and conduct an investigation. Hassan's complaint names Priya as well as Can Channel Media owner Sukumar and interviewer Suresh. She has alleged that they portrayed her as 'a woman of immoral character' and thereby committed offences under Sections 75 (iv) (sexual harassment) and 79 (outraging modesty of a woman) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS). Advocates Muhammed Firdouz AV and Libin Varghese represented Ansiba Hassan.

items.title: Supreme Court seeks NIA response to bail plea of man accused of links to Dawood Ibrahim’s gang
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday issued notice on a bail plea filed by a man accused of helping the gang led by terrorist Dawood Ibrahim extort money and move funds through hawala routes [ Shabbir Abubakar Shaikh v. National Investigation Agency ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta sought the National Investigation Agency’s (NIA) response to a plea filed by Shabbir Abubakar Shaikh challenging a Bombay High Court order that refused him bail. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The NIA alleges that Shaikh acted on instructions from Dawood Ibrahim and Chhota Shakeel and helped extort ₹16 crores from a protected witness between 2008 and 2018. It also claims he received ₹25 lakhs through hawala routes in April 2022, kept ₹5 lakhs and passed the remaining ₹20 lakhs to another accused. The agency alleges that the money was intended for terrorist and criminal activities. Shaikh disputes his alleged links to the gang and denies that the money was meant for terrorism. He has also challenged the application of the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999 (MCOCA) to his case. A special NIA court rejected his bail plea in December 2024. The Bombay High Court upheld that decision on April 15, 2026, finding that the material prima facie indicated a link between Shaikh and the alleged organised crime syndicate. Shaikh then approached the Supreme Court. Advocate Mehmood Pracha , appearing for Shaikh, told the Court that his client had been in custody for more than four years, but charges had yet to be framed. “ My Lords, four years have elapsed; an 8,000-page chargesheet. Charges have not been framed, ” Pracha submitted. “ Since when have you been in custody ?” Justice Nath asked. “ May of 2022. Four years, four months. 137 witnesses, 8,000 pages of chargesheet, ” Pracha replied. Additional Solicitor General (ASG) SV Raju , appearing for the NIA, said he would file a detailed response. “ But he’s a member of the Dawood gang ,” Raju submitted. ASG SV Raju Pracha, however, disputed that allegation and said he would address the applicability of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (UAPA) when the matter is heard further. Mehmood Pracha After hearing the preliminary submissions, the Court issued notice to the NIAand granted the agency four weeks to file its response. Advocates RHA Sikander, Jatin Bhatt, Sanawar, Vipin Kumar, Nikhil Guliani, Nujhat Naseem, Kumail Abbas, and Adeel Hassan also represented Shaikh.

items.title: Collegium should include President’s nominee, Attorney General: Retired Justice Pankaj Mithal
items.summary: The Supreme Court collegium should be expanded to include a nominee of the President of India, the Attorney General for India and an independent constitutional functionary to improve transparency and restore public confidence in judicial appointments, former Supreme Court Justice Pankaj Mithal said on Thursday. Speaking in Hindi, at the fifth edition of Nyay Nirman @ 2047: Building the Legal Architecture of India’s Global Future , Justice Mithal said reform of the judicial appointments process was among the most urgent changes required as India looks towards becoming a developed nation by 2047. “ However, we must candidly acknowledge that the Collegium system is an extra-constitutional authority that we created. While it was established with good intentions, it now requires substantial improvement, ” he said. Justice Mithal proposed expanding the Supreme Court collegium to seven members. Apart from judges, he said, the sixth member could be an eminent person nominated by the President or the Attorney General for India, who represents both the bar and the government. The seventh member could be a distinguished constitutional post-holder nominated by the President, such as the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), he suggested. He said, “If a seven-member body sits together and makes selections, public confidence in the appointment process will be substantially restored. People will feel that the process is inclusive, that the Bar has a voice, and that independent constitutional authorities are contributing alongside the senior judiciary .” Justice Mithal said the Law Ministry, Supreme Court and other stakeholders should seriously deliberate on the proposal. He also called for parity in the retirement ages of High Court and Supreme Court judges by fixing both at 65 years. Justice Mithal further questioned the practice of appointing Chief Justices of High Courts for very short tenures. “ Appointing someone as a Chief Justice just ahead of retirement to confer post-retirement benefits is not a sound practice, ” he said. The appeal against the magistrate court's order of August 3 is likely to be heard by the sessions judge on Saturday. items.title: Supreme Court refuses to halt forensic audit of Fortis transactions in Daiichi-Singh brothers dispute

However, a Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified that the High Court's observations against Fortis were only tentative and prima facie and would not bind the forensic auditor. items.title: Aren't you treating him as accused? Supreme Court questions Odisha for excluding IPS officer from DGP selection

items.title: Centre reappoints K Arvind Kamath, B Narsimha Sharma as ASGs in Karnataka, Telangana High Courts
items.summary: The Central government has reappointed Senior Advocates K Arvind Kamath and B Narsimha Sharma as Additional Solicitors General (ASGs) to represent it before the High Courts of Karnataka and Telangana, respectively. The reappointments were notified on September 23. They have been re-appointed for a three-year period with effect from October 17, 2026, or until further orders, whichever is earlier. Arvind Kamath obtained his Bachelor of Laws degree from JSS Law College, Mysuru, in 1992. He subsequently pursued a Master of Laws (LLM) from the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru (NLSIU). He enrolled as an advocate in 1993, and initially practised before the City Civil Court, Bengaluru. From 1995-96 onwards, he has primarily practised before the Karnataka High Court. In 2000, Kamath was awarded the British Chevening Scholarship by the British Council, under which he underwent training in English and European Union commercial and corporate laws. Kamath has also been associated with legal education. He taught for around 12 years and served as guest faculty at MS Ramaiah Law College. In 2003, he was appointed Assistant Editor of the Indian Law Reports by the Karnataka High Court. In November 2018, Kamath was designated as a Senior Advocate by the Karnataka High Court. On October 17, 2023 , the government of India appointed Kamath as an ASG to represent the Central government before the High Court of Karnataka. By the same notification, the Centre also appointed B Narsimha Sharma as an ASG to represent it before the Telangana High Court. Sharma was designated a Senior Advocate towards the end of 2022. items.title: Journalist Ravi Nair moves Supreme Court against arrest in Adani defamation case
items.summary: Journalist Ravi Nair has approached the Supreme Court seeking release from prison in connection with a criminal defamation case filed against him by the Adani Group Nair, who was convicted in the case earlier this year, had been released on bail during the pendency of his appeal, but was again taken into custody on September 17 following the issuance of a non-bailable warrant against him for not appearing before the appellate court. In February, a magistrate convicted Nair in a criminal defamation case filed by the Adani Group in connection with a series of tweets and online articles accusing the Adani Group of numerous unethical practices. The Court ruled that the content went beyond fair criticism and amounted to criminal defamation. The case stemmed from a criminal complaint filed by the Adani Group in September 2021. The company alleged that between October 2020 and July 2021, Nair published multiple tweets from his X (formerly Twitter) handle and articles on a website called “adaniwatch.org”, accusing the Adani Group corruption, crony capitalism, manipulation of environmental laws, misuse of government agencies and unethical business practices. Following his conviction, he filed an appeal before a sessions court to challenge the verdict delivered by the judicial magistrate. The Court released him on bail during the pendency of the appeal. However, since he failed to appear before the Court earlier this month, a non-bailable warrant was issued against him. Nair then appeared before the sessions court and challenged the issuance of the non-bailable warrant. However, the Court rejected his plea and sent him to judicial custody. He then moved the High Court seeking immediate release from custody. Justice MK Thakker of Gujarat High Court heard the matter and reserved her verdict but declined to release him in the interim . The Court said it will pronounce the order on September 30, Wednesday. When Nair's counsel pressed for interim release, the High Court said, "As this matter has been heard and the matter is kept for dictation of the order, no interim relief is required to be granted." items.title: Muraleedharan G Vallakkadavu elected Bar Council of Kerala chairman, Girija K Gopal is vice-chairperson
items.summary: Advocates Muraleedharan G Vallakkadavu and Girija K Gopal have been elected chairperson and Vice-Chairperson respectively of the bar Council of Kerala (BCK). Vallakkadavu was among the 23 advocates elected to the Council in the elections held on April 17 this year. The Bar Council of Kerala is a statutory body constituted under the Advocates Act, 1961, which regulates the enrolment and professional conduct of advocates in the state. The polls were held for 23 of the 25 seats in the Council across 84 polling centres, with a mandatory 30 percent quota for women, following interim directions issued by the Supreme Court of India. The election was supervised by a high-powered election committee pursuant to the directions of the Supreme Court in M Vardhan v Union of India & Anr, to ensure fairness in the process. Retired Justice VG Arun of the Kerala High Court served as the returning officer to oversee the election process. After counting of votes concluded on May 13, Justice Arun submitted the names of the 23 elected members to the committee. The other elected members include advocates Santhosh Kumar P, Nagaraj Narayanan, Manoj Kumar N, Pramod SK, Mohammed Shafi M, Mujeeb Rehuman A, Yeshwanth L, Nasseer KK, Sree Prakash P, Jayachandran KP, Jayadeep M, Jaya PM, Manoj S, Anil Kumar N, Anil S Raj, Jos Mechery, Sudarsanakumar S, Sajeev Babu P, Sheela Devi I, Geena Kumary T, Geetha Kumary VP and Preethi Parambath. Gopal became a member of the Council through co-option. Kerala High Court Chief Justice Soumen Sen nominated Gopal as woman member of the Kerala Bar Council. The nomination followed Supreme Court’s directions concerning representation of women in State Bar Councils. Advocate Jos Mechery has been elected as the Treasurer, while advocate Santhosh Kumar P has been elected as the Council's representative to the Bar Council of India. Elections to the statutory committee are still underway. items.title: Madras High Court dismisses PIL which said resigning MLA should pay bye-election expenses
items.summary: The Madras High Court has dismissed a public interest litigation (PIL) petition that had urged it to direct the Election Commission of India (ECI) to introduce a mechanism requiring legislators who voluntarily resign from their seats to bear the expenses of resulting by-elections [ Suthan Vs Union of India ]. The petitioner had also called for a five-year ban on such resigning legislators from contesting in elections State Assembly or Parliament elections. A Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan , however, observed that these are not domains where the judiciary should intervene. "We are being asked to design a punitive and financial regime that would operate as a fresh disqualification under the Constitution of India and would curtail the statutory right to contest an election. In our considered opinion, the same is a matter of legislative policy, not of judicial direction," it said. CJ SA Dharmadhikari and Justice Arul Murugan In this regard, the Court noted that neither the Constitution of India nor the Representation of the People Act, 1951, presently imposes such punitive consequences on legislators who resign. “ The right to resign a legislative seat is itself a facet of the constitutional scheme governing membership of a House, and cannot be burdened with extra-statutory conditions by judicial order, however sound the underlying concern may be," it held. The PIL before the Court was filed by advocate K Suthan after six AIADMK MLAs elected in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections resigned from their seats shortly after the results. They resigned after defying the AIADMK whip to express support for the TVK-led State government on the floor of the Tamil Nadu Assembly during a confidence vote held in May. After their resignations, they also joined the TVK party. Their resignations, meanwhile, necessitated the conduct of by-elections in the six constituencies they had earlier won elections from. The petitioner before the High Court sought the creation of an “Election Expenditure Security” mechanism, under which an MLA who prematurely resigns and subsequently wishes to contest the resulting by-election would first have to deposit an amount equal to the public money spent on conducting that by-election. He argued that taxpayers should not be required to pay twice for an election to the same seat merely because its representative chose to resign. items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday reserved its verdict on a plea by former Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin Thachankary for the suspension of his 4-year jail sentence in a disproportionate assets case [ Tomin J Thachakary v. State of Kerala ]. Thachankary has sought a suspension of his jail sentence until his appeal against the trial court's conviction and sentence against him is decided by the High Court. Justice A Badharudeen today reserved his verdict on this question of interim relief. items.title: Judicial process must provide remedy, not merely identify litigant's wound: Madras High Court
items.summary: The judicial process is meant not merely to identify a litigant’s “wound” but also to provide a remedy for it, the Madras High Court recently observed. [Muthulakshmi v. Raju] A Division Bench of Justices N Anand Venkatesh and KK Ramakrishnan said that courts must keep in mind the human dimension of litigation and ensure that procedural law does not become a means to postpone, dilute or ultimately deny substantive justice. "The judicial process is intended not merely to identify the existence of a wound but also to provide the legally permissible remedy for its redressal." The Bench added that courts exist to render substantive justice and that procedural complexities cannot be allowed to defeat lawful rights. Justices Anand Venkatesh and KK Ramakrishnan The Court was dealing with a commercial appeal arising from a prolonged partnership dispute in which the litigant had moved through multiple civil and arbitration proceedings without her substantive claims being adjudicated on merits. Where proceedings are terminated on an erroneous legal premise without deciding the actual controversy, merely directing the litigant to pursue another remedy, particularly one which is not statutorily applicable, would not advance the cause of justice, the Bench said. Referring to Justice VR Krishna Iyer's observation that “litigants are legal patients suffering from injustices seeking healing for their wounds ”, the High Court stressed that courts must ultimately provide effective redress rather than leave litigants trapped in procedural loops. It referred to Supreme Court precedent recognising that where the existing statutory framework does not readily provide a just answer, courts may resort to principles of justice, equity and good conscience to fairly resolve disputes. The Court noted that equity could supplement the law in appropriate cases and enable courts to craft relief that is both legally sustainable and just. The Bench said that behind procedural complications, interlocutory delays and successive rounds of litigation failed an elderly litigant who had been seeking adjudication of her claimed rights for years. “ The cumulative weight of these procedural vicissitudes and the continuing litigation has prolonged her struggle far beyond what justice should ordinarily demand ,” the Court observed. items.title: Delhi High Court asks Centre to decide SFI's plea against Instagram  account blocking
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday asked the Central government's grievance appellate committee (GAC) to decide the Students' Federation of India (SFI) appeal against the blocking of its Instagram account. Justice Amit Mahajan said that he expects the SFI's appeal to be decided in three weeks. SFI is the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). The court passed the order on a plea filed by SFI. Advocate Apar Gupta appeared for the student organisation and stated the statutory time period prescribed to decide such an appeal is four weeks. He said the Court had previously disposed off similar matters with direction to the government to decide the appeal in an additional four weeks. The Court recorded that the SFI had filed the appeal before the government on August 12 and no order has been passed till date. It then disposed of the plea, asking the government to decide the appeal. According to SFI, Instagram permanently disabled the SFI Delhi account on July 5, stating that it “may be associated with another account that has gone against our rules” and therefore did not comply with its community standards on account integrity. SFI stated that Instagram did not disclose any further particulars or identify the allegedly associated account. The account, created in 2018, had around 13,000 followers. The students' body said they first appealed against the action on July 7 and subsequently approached Meta's grievance officer on July 9. However, they received no response, following which they approached the GAC on August 12. As of September 16, the GAC website showed the appeal as “under process”, despite more than 30 days having elapsed, the petition stated. The petitioner relied on Rule 3A(4) of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 which requires the GAC to deal with appeals expeditiously and endeavour to resolve them finally within 30 calendar days. It also sought a direction to the GAC to conduct its appeal process in conformity with the fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed under Articles 14, 19(1)(a), 19(1)(g), and 21. items.title: Husband's girlfriend cannot be booked for cruelty to wife under Section 85 BNS: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed criminal proceedings against a woman paramour who was accused of ruining the married relationship of a couple and intimidating the wife. Justice M Nagaprasanna said that the law is settled that a paramour cannot be accused of the offence of cruelty against wife against Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) since she is not a relative of the husband. In this regard, the Court relied on the Supreme Court's decision in Dechamma IM @ Dechamma Koushik v State of Karnataka in which it was held that a girlfriend of a married man cannot be construed as his relative. "In the light of the bedrock of the law elucidated by the Apex Court, if the facts obtaining in the case at hand are observed, a paramour of the husband - accused No.1 cannot be termed as a relative of the husband," it said. Justice M Nagaprasanna The petitioner (paramour) had approached the High Court after a trial court took cognizance of a criminal case registered against her. The complaint alleged offences of subjecting the wife to cruelty, assault or use of criminal force against her, intentional insult, and criminal intimidation under the BNS. It also accused her of the offence of taking dowry under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. The High Court said none of offences are made out against the petitioner and quashed the proceedings against her. Advocates Gagandeep E and Ajit PB appeared for the petitioner. High Court Government Pleader Rashmi Patel represented the State. Advocate PM Gopi appeared for the wife. items.title: Supreme Court shifting to ecocentric approach; no automatic precedence for human interests: Justice BV Nagarathna
items.summary: The Supreme Court is pushing for a shift from an anthropocentric to an ecocentric approach in environmental cases, Justice BV Nagarathna recently said. Under ecocentric approach, human interests would not automatically take precedence over those of the non-human world, she explained. “This entails recognising that human interests do not, by virtue of being human, enjoy automatic precedence over the interests of the non-human world; rather, we bear obligations towards non-human life that exist independently of their utility to us,” she said. The judge was speaking at the valedictory session of the National Green Tribunal’s International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”. Justice Nagarathna said environmental adjudication require courts to look beyond completed violations and deal with risks that were unfolding in real time, often amid scientific uncertainty and with potentially irreversible consequences. “In that sense, environmental adjudication is an exercise in foresight, requiring courts to govern the present with an alert consciousness of the future,” she said. Justice Nagarathna also said environmental that justice requires courts and governments to account for the fact that environmental decisions affect regions, communities and generations differently. Since environmental issues are increasingly crossing national boundaries, cooperation between nations has become necessary to address pollution, climate change, biodiversity loss and degradation of shared ecosystems, she opined. “Good environmental governance, therefore, requires not only rights, but effective institutions, enforcement, transparency, accountability and access to justice,” the judge remarked. items.title: From granite pioneer to POCSO accused: The unravelling of mining baron R Veeramani
items.summary: “R Veeramani is senior-most exporter of granite in India, he is having offices in 86 countries… he’s a top-most businessman… one of the finest gentlemen supporting this movement (sic).” This gushing introduction to R Veeramani was made at a 2017 World Tamil Economic Conference in Durban by its president, VRS Sampath, and is typical of the public image the businessman used to enjoy: a pioneer of the country’s granite export sector, a well-networked entrepreneur, the head of multiple industry chambers and a member of government bodies. His arrest in late August exposed a much darker side: the octogenarian now stands accused of sexually assaulting a minor. After his arrest, more survivors, mostly from marginalised backgrounds, have come forward with similar accusations against him and the police have widened the probe. When contacted, some former business acquaintances said they were astonished at the recent allegations against Veeramani. “Everyone is shocked at the case,” said Ishwinder Singh, president, Federation of Indian Granite and Stone Industry (FIGSI) – an organisation Veeramani founded in 1983. Many others in the industry declined to comment. items.title: Veeramani case: Meeting the NGO that handed the video to cops | The News Minute
items.summary: The case against Gem Granites founder R Veeramani has raised serious questions about how allegations of sexual abuse of minors were handled by the Chennai Police. A complaint alleging sexual abuse against minor by Veeramani and his associate Shanthi was submitted in November 2024 by a Congress functionary MP Ranjan Kumar. However, the case was formally registered only in October 2025, after a pen drive containing a video showing a minor being sexually assaulted was handed over to the Anti-Vice Squad. In February 2026, the police filed a report seeking to drop further action, citing difficulties including identifying the girl in the video. In this interview, Shabbir Ahmed speaks to AJ Hariharan, Secretary of ICWO, about the pen drive and letter that reached the organisation, its decision to report the material to the police, and the questions surrounding the attempted closure of the case.

items.title: Four-member all-woman SIT formed to probe Veeramani POCSO case
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu Police on Thursday, September 24, formed a four-member all-woman Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the child sexual assault case and related allegations against Gem Group of Companies chairman R Veeramani, amid scrutiny of the handling of the earlier probe. Director-General of Police Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal ordered the formation of the SIT, which will be headed by Additional Commissioner of Police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch. Joint Commissioner Disha Mittal, Superintendent of Police J Mutharasi, and Superintendent of Police VV Geethanjali are the other members. The formation of the SIT came on the same day that action was taken against three police officers involved in the earlier probe. Additional Director General of Police A Arun and Inspector General of Police/Commissioner of Police, Coimbatore City N Kannan were placed under compulsory wait at the office of the DGP. Assistant Commissioner MA Yasmin of the Koyambedu Range was transferred to the Chief Office Vacancy Reserve on administrative grounds. The action against the officers came amid questions over the handling of the POCSO complaint against Veeramani. Hours before this, TNM had reported that Tamil Nadu Congress Committee's Scheduled Caste wing president MP Ranjan Kumar had earlier approached then Additional Commissioner of Police N Kannan with a complaint against Veeramani in November 2024. Kannan had told TNM that he escalated the matter to the then Chennai Police Commissioner A Arun. The case was registered in October 2025 after a child welfare volunteer approached the Anti-Vice Squad of the Chennai police with a pen drive containing a video that purportedly showed a minor girl being sexually assaulted. The volunteer said an unidentified person had handed over the storage device and claimed that the video showed Veeramani allegedly committing a sexual offence against a minor at the house of his associate Shanthi. The police examined the video and subsequently registered a case. However, the initial investigation did not result in Veeramani's arrest. In February 2026, the police submitted a report seeking to close the case, citing lack of evidence and difficulties in establishing the identity and whereabouts of the minor girl.
